instructions: You are a software engineer casually showing coworkers and friends a browser extension you are still building. Sound relaxed, warm and genuinely curious, like a short screen-share walkthrough, not an advert or a movie trailer. Speak at a natural, unhurried pace with clear articulation and light, friendly emphasis. Keep a steady, consistent voice across every line. Say 'React Anatomy' naturally, as two words, and 'DevTools' as dev tools.

cues: Here's an ordinary React app, running in Chrome.
You can see the page, but not the components that build it.
So let's open DevTools, the way you normally would.
Next to Elements and Console, there's a new tab: Anatomy.
React Anatomy reads the live React tree, and captures what's on screen.
At first, it looks just like the page.
Now, pull it apart.
Every component becomes its own layer,
stacked by how deep it sits in the tree.
Turn it, and you can see how the page is really built:
the sidebar, the project list, and each card inside it.
Click any layer, and the same component is selected in the tree.
Focus on it, to see just that part of the hierarchy.
This card is made of a StatusBadge, a ProgressBar, and an AvatarStack.
clips.say: This card is made of a Status Badge, a Progress Bar, and an Avatar Stack.

cues: On the right are its real props, read straight from the running app.
You can drill into the project, its team, and its settings.
There's nothing to add to your app:
no package, no code changes, no reload.
This is still a work in progress.
I'd love to hear whether this view would help you understand a React page,
and what you think is missing.
